display.purpose: Page titles on single-column routes. Fluid: 26px on a phone, 36px on a wide desktop.

headline.purpose: The detail pane's thread title — the largest element in the three-pane view. Drops to 23px below 820px.

title.purpose: Card headers, history items, detail cards. Section cards run one step up at 18px.

body.purpose: All reading text. Always capped with a ch measure — 68ch descriptions, 46ch empty states.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, rail headings, table headers, source-box labels. Uppercase; the 0.09em tracking is what makes 11px readable at weight 750.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: Every card, stat tile, and composer panel at rest. TARGET value — the shipped --shadow-sm is 0 1px 2px rgba(23,35,28,0.04), effectively invisible.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on an interactive card, selected list row, active nav item. A state response, never a resting condition.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Things that leave the page: filter menu, mobile drawer, dialogs. Matches the shipped --shadow-md geometry at higher opacity.

shadows.name: entry-exception
shadows.purpose: The signed-out entry card only. Sanctioned exception: it floats over a gradient with nothing else on screen.

shadows.name: shipped-shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: As-built --shadow-sm. Recorded for accuracy; too faint to read as depth. Migrate to `rest`.

shadows.name: shipped-shadow-md
shadows.purpose: As-built --shadow-md, used on the mobile drawer panel and sign-in card. Migrate to `float`.

motion.name: button-transition
motion.purpose: The only transition in the system. Buttons only, background only.

motion.name: reduced-motion-kill
motion.purpose: Global override. All transitions and animations are removed for users who ask for it — a hard invariant, not a nicety.

narrative.overview:
A shared working room, not a brochure and not a spreadsheet. Staff and students use the same room from different doors: a persistent left rail carrying courses and categories, a dense middle list of real submissions, and a detail pane where one thing gets read properly. The tools in it are worn-in and practical — plain-spoken labels, honest counts, thin rules — with just enough warmth that a student about to type an uncomfortable truth doesn't feel like they're filing a ticket.

Warmth here is scoped, not global. Student-facing surfaces (the weekly form, section home, history) get the generous padding, softer corners, and gentle focus treatment that make an honest complaint easier to write. Staff surfaces (review, participation, audit, matches) keep their density: a teacher triaging a week of submissions needs rows they can scan, not cushions. Both live under the same tokens; only the breathing room differs.

The implemented world is a light warm-neutral canvas (#f5f7f2) with deep ink text (#17231c), separated by 1px hairlines rather than heavy containers. It carries three accents in three zones — a documented accident, not a plan. Nothing is generated, illustrated, or animated for its own sake: the codebase's own comment on rail counts — "real count only — never a decorative number" — is the whole aesthetic in one line.

Confirmed rejections: no third-party logo, product name, brand color, or asset is reproduced. Ed Discussion, Piazza, and Slido informed the information architecture only; the result must not read as any of them with the logo removed. No dark mode exists.
keyCharacteristics: Three-pane workspace chrome (rail → list → detail) on every signed-in route
System font stack only; no webfonts, no font loading cost
Hairline borders as the primary separator; color used sparingly and by role
Status always carries text and a distinct shape, never color alone
Chrome that works without client JavaScript (<details> for drawer and filter)
Real data or an empty state — never filler, never a decorative number

rules.name: The Three-Zone Rule
rules.body: The system currently runs three accents in three zones: plum owns the chrome (top bar, entry screen), blue owns navigation (rail, links, list selection), green owns content actions (buttons, badges, focus, form state). This is recorded as observed fact, not as design intent — it is the residue of a green academic palette from docs/UX-DESIGN-BRIEF.md being wrapped in a later workspace chrome. Until someone consolidates it, respect the zoning strictly: a green button inside plum chrome is the existing convention, but introducing a fourth accent, or using blue for a content action, or green for chrome, makes the incoherence worse. Consolidation is an open decision, not a license to freestyle.

rules.name: The Red Reserve Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for destruction, invalid input, privacy risk, or failure. Never for emphasis, never for a count, never for a category, never for a brand moment. If red is on screen, something is either irreversible or wrong.

rules.name: The Wash-Plus-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every role color ships as a triple: the base hue for solid fills, an -ink step for text, and a -soft wash for backgrounds. Colored text always sits on its own wash using the ink step, never the base hue on white and never white on the wash. Adding a role color means adding all three.

rules.name: The Whole-Pixel Rule
rules.body: The workspace chrome layer contains fractional sizes — 10.5px, 11.5px, 12.5px, 13.5px, 14.5px, 15.5px. These are drift, not craft, and they subpixel differently across platforms. New type must land on whole pixels, and existing fractional values should be normalized to the nearest step when a file is touched anyway.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Any block of prose a human reads end-to-end carries a max-width in ch, not px: 68ch for descriptions, 46ch for centered empty states, 34–40ch for hero ledes. Unbounded body text is a defect.

rules.name: The Drawer-Not-Disappear Rule
rules.body: Navigation never simply vanishes at a breakpoint. The rail becomes a keyboard-openable <details> drawer; the current section and role stay visible in the top bar. Any new persistent navigation must have a small-screen home.

rules.name: The No-JS Chrome Rule
rules.body: The mobile drawer and the list filter are native <details>/<summary> disclosures, and search is a plain GET form. The chrome therefore works before hydration and with client JavaScript unavailable. New chrome affordances should hold this line; save client state for genuinely interactive editors.

rules.name: The URL-Is-The-Selection Rule
rules.body: Which row is selected, which category filters the list, and which pane shows on a phone are all derived from the URL, not from component state. Selection is shareable and survives reload.

rules.name: The Float-Earns-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadow depth maps to literal stacking, not to importance. A card is Rest because it lies on the page; a menu is Float because it covers what's beneath it. Never reach for a heavier shadow to make something feel more important — that's what type and color are for.

dos: Do keep the global focus treatment (3px solid #0e6044, 2px offset) on every interactive element. The stylesheet says "Never remove it"; that is a hard invariant.
Do communicate every status with text and shape and color. Use Badge / CycleStateBadge rather than a bare colored dot.
Do render only real counts. A count pill, a stat tile, or a notification badge with a placeholder number is a defect — the code's own rule is "real count only — never a decorative number."
Do respect the Three-Zone Rule: plum for chrome, blue for navigation, green for content actions.
Do cap prose with a ch measure (68ch descriptions, 46ch empty states).
Do give every new persistent navigation a small-screen drawer home, and build chrome affordances with <details> so they work without client JS.
Do pair a soft wash background with its -ink text step whenever color carries meaning.
Do keep the original student wording visibly quoted and recessed wherever staff act on it. Never present a reworded version as if it were the original.
Do land new type sizes on whole pixels.
donts: Don't reproduce any third-party logo, product name, brand color, asset, or exact copy — Ed Discussion, Piazza, and Slido are architecture references and explicit anti-references.
Don't introduce a fourth accent color, or cross the zones (no blue primary buttons, no green chrome).
Don't use red for anything but destruction, invalid input, privacy risk, or failure.
Don't use shadow to signal importance. Shadow maps to literal stacking only.
Don't ship a card, stat, or list without its 1px hairline border; borders carry the structure even once shadows are real.
Don't add fractional font sizes (13.5px, 15.5px). Normalize existing ones when touching the file.
Don't show student-authored text on a staff surface without a visible marker for whether it is private or public.

Don't add a webfont, a dark mode, or an animation library without an explicit decision — the system currently has none of the three, and prefers-reduced-motion: reduce globally kills all transitions and animations.

Don't revive the superseded green shell layer (.app-frame, .app-sidebar, .page-shell, .signin-frame, .signin-layout, .review-layout, .archive-layout, .qa-row, .answer-panel, .nav-item, .mobile-nav). Those classes are still in globals.css but no component renders them; every route now goes through WorkspaceShell. Reusing them reintroduces a second shell.
